newsitem.title: USA: N.J. official says to forbid eminent domain tactic.
newsitem.headline: N.J. official says to forbid eminent domain tactic.

text.p: New Jersey will prevent local bond issuers from using eminent domain as a method of calling bonds early without paying a penalty, a state official said.
Several local entities in recent months have sparked controversy in the municipal bond market by using eminent domain to condemn buildings financed by certificates of participation.
The governments then invoked clauses in lease purchase agreements allowing an early call without penalty in the event of condemnation.

But James Verner, supervising auditor at the state's Department of Education, said in a telephone interview that New Jersey as a matter of policy would no longer approve lease purchase agreements containing such language.
"When any lease purchase agreement comes across, we will look to see that that clause has to be excluded," Verner said.

Verner said the policy change was legally unnecessary, since a recent Superior Court ruling on one of the cases found that COPs issuers must pay the call premium if they call the debt early through condemnation.
The ruling, decided last month against Harmony, N.J.'s Board of Education, agreed with debt holders, who argued the condemnation provision was never intended to be used in this manner.
Market participants upset over the tactic boycotted attempts to sell debt by the Pinelands and Little Egg Harbor school districts, which also tried to use eminent domain to call debt early.
